subject: Post-call recap + proposed rotating demo windows (next steps)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy@medisys.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed rotating demo windows (next steps)

Hi Amy — thanks again for the time today, appreciate the clear context. Quick recap from our side so we’re all aligned and can lock the next step (technical deep dive / infra pairing):

Key takeaways from the discovery call:
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency for customer-facing features while keeping costs within existing SLOs.
- Constraint: some PHI flows require Private deployment (VPC) and customer-supplied KMS.
- Scale: pilot ~200 concurrent users, long-term growth projected ~5x.
- Success metrics you called out: 95th pct token latency under 300ms (EU/US), clear audit logs, and predictable monthly TCO.

Next step we recommend: 60-minute technical deep dive with your infra architect + our runtime engineer to validate network/VPC requirements, sample payloads, and an initial throughput test plan.

Because your engineering team is distributed, we put together three rotating-slot approaches (attached: availability_matrix_v2.xlsx) so the deep dive can alternate between US-friendly, EU-friendly, and APAC-friendly times across weekly runs. High-level options (pick one or tell us tweaks):

Option Alpha — 6-week rotating baton (minimal timezone pain)
- Week 1: US window (PDT 10:00 / EDT 13:00) — 60m deep dive (synchronous with US PMs)
- Week 2: EU window (CEST 15:00 / BST 14:00)
- Week 3: APAC window (AEST 09:00 / SGT 07:00)
- Repeat for Weeks 4–6 (so each region sees two sessions over 6 weeks).

Option Beta — twice-weekly overlap (faster iteration, shorter sessions)
- Tue: US/EU overlap (UTC-friendly 15:00) — 45m emphasis on infra & networking
- Thu: EU/APAC overlap (UTC-friendly 02:00) — 45m (recorded for US folks)

Option Gamma — fixed mid-week UTC pivot (consistent time for global stakeholders)
- Weekly Wed 14:00 UTC (rotating roster of attendees per week; sessions recorded)

Ask: please confirm which option you prefer, and who from your infra/security side should be on the invite (we typically include a runtime engineer, PM, and solutions engineer). If none of these look good, tell us 2–3 specific local windows that work and we’ll map into a rotation.

I’ve also included a short demo brief (redwood-demo-brief.pdf) so you can share it internally. Calendly link below if you prefer to pick a specific slot: https://calendly.com/redwood/vivek-demo-60

Thanks — happy to iterate on timing.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Amy Chen <amy@medisys.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 20:05:00 +08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed rotating demo windows (next steps)

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. This map is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- We definitely need the VPC/KMS conversation in the deep dive — I’ll loop in our infra lead (Carlos Romero) once we lock a time.
- Ideally sessions are 60 minutes. Our engineering team prefers mid-week if possible (Tue-Thu).
- For APAC, mornings (SGT/AEST) are easiest for our Hong Kong and Sydney folks; for EU they prefer early afternoon CEST.

Option Alpha looks closest to what we want, but can we start the first session in an EU window (CEST afternoon) so our EU stakeholders can validate requirements before the US pilot?

I can join the EU session and will add Carlos to the thread after I confirm with him later today. I’ll reply with Carlos’ availability in the next message.

— Amy
Amy Chen
Head of Platform & Integrations
MediSys Health
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy@medisys.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed rotating demo windows (next steps)

Amy — thanks, that’s helpful. Based on Amy’s preference to start with an EU session, we propose this concrete 6-week cadence that keeps the rotation symmetric while honoring mid-week windows. I’ve included local equivalents so you can forward to Carlos/infra folks without mental conversions. Attach: availability_matrix_v2.xlsx (updated)

Proposed 6-week schedule (Option Alpha, EU-first):
- Week A (Wk 1) — Wed 21 Jul 2027 — EU session — 15:00 CEST (45:00–16:00 BST) / 14:00 BST — 60m
- Week B (Wk 2) — Wed 28 Jul 2027 — US session — 10:00 PDT / 13:00 EDT — 60m
- Week C (Wk 3) — Wed 04 Aug 2027 — APAC session — 09:00 AEST / 07:00 SGT — 60m
- Week D (Wk 4) — Wed 11 Aug 2027 — EU session (repeat) — 15:00 CEST — 60m
- Week E (Wk 5) — Wed 18 Aug 2027 — US session — 10:00 PDT — 60m
- Week F (Wk 6) — Wed 25 Aug 2027 — APAC session — 09:00 AEST — 60m

Logistics we’ll provide once timing is locked:
- Zoom link + dial-in (we’ll post a dedicated meeting room for the series)
- A short runbook for the session (sample payloads, network test checklist).
- A read-only HubSpot note attached to DEAL MS-8841 so your CS/Procurement team can see progress: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/58431/MS-8841

Fallback: if a particular week’s roster is heavy on US participants and APAC can’t attend live, we’ll record and run a 30-minute async review the following day for APAC engineers to validate the outcomes.

Please confirm (A) that Carlos can join the EU session on Wed 21 Jul 2027 15:00 CEST and (B) who else from infra/security should be on the invite. If confirmed, I’ll create a recurring series with calendar invites and include the runbook + Zoom.

— Priyom
